paras: The attempted lynching of Melved H. Rosier was a failed attempt by masked men on the night of Saturday, October 3, 1903, to lynch a Black boy of about fifteen held in the county jail at La Plata, Charles County, Maryland. The jail officer took Rosier out of the jail shortly before the mob came, hid him in the woods overnight and moved him to a place of safety the next day. Two Washington-area papers reported the episode as a frustrated lynching on October 6.

Rosier, described as a "colored boy," worked for W. B. S. Chapman, who lived near La Plata. According to the Alexandria Gazette, he was arrested on the Thursday before the attempt, charged with attempted assault on Chapman's four-year-old daughter.

At about 9:30 on Saturday night, the jailer took Rosier out of the county jail, the Gazette reported. Around 10 o'clock a masked mob came to lynch him, but the prisoner was already gone. The Evening Star, citing "a report from La Plata," gave the attackers as "a party of masked men" and credited the warden with removing the "youthful prisoner" in time to frustrate the plan. Rosier spent the night in the woods near La Plata and was moved to a place of safety on Sunday.
Neither report named any member of the masked party or mentioned arrests, and no later report of Rosier's trial or of the charge's outcome was found in the coverage.

The episode appeared in two white papers on Tuesday, October 6, 1903, both on page 2. The Washington Evening Star ran it under "Lynching Attempted" with a deck about the plans of a "Necktle [Necktie] Party" being "Frustrated," and hedged the mob's presence with "it was reported." The Alexandria Gazette's shorter item, headed "Lynchers After Negro Boy," stated the attempt flatly and added the hours and the date of arrest. Both papers treated the charge as a charge, calling Rosier "the accused" or "the youthful prisoner," and neither commented on the mob; no Black-press account was found.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Melved H. Rosier
bases: A masked party tried to take a jailed Black boy and lynch him, and the attempt failed because the jail officer removed him first (A1, A2).

Rosier was not killed: the jail officer removed him before the masked men arrived, and he was taken to safety (A1, A2). The papers describe an attempted lynching by a 'party of masked men' or 'masked mob' acting on a charge of attempted assault, with no number given (A1, A2).

Two Washington-area papers on the same day agree on the victim, charge, masked party, removal from jail and outcome; A2 adds details A1 lacks, so the two may share a source but are not identical texts (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Report from La Plata
accounts.gist: A party of masked men tried Saturday night to lynch the boy, but the warden had already removed him from the jail; he spent the night in the woods and was moved to safety Sunday. The mob's presence is given as 'it was reported'.

accounts.label: Alexandria Gazette item
accounts.gist: States flatly that a masked mob tried at 10 o'clock to lynch Rosier, after the jailer had taken him out at about 9:30; adds the Thursday arrest.

framing.detail: The Evening Star headed it 'Lynching Attempted' with a deck about a 'Necktle [Necktie] Party' frustrated, gave the charge as a charge, and called Rosier a 'youthful prisoner'.
The Alexandria Gazette headed it 'Lynchers After Negro Boy' and called Rosier 'the accused'; no editorial comment.

conflicts.note: Probably the same officer described with different titles; neither paper names him.

versions.value: 'it was reported' that masked men made the attempt
stated as fact: 'by a masked mob'

conflicts.note: Differs in hedging only, not in substance.

record_check.dossier: Black: both papers call Rosier a 'colored boy'; A2's headline says 'Negro Boy'
Neither paper reports arms or a siege of the jail; the masked men's attempt was forestalled by the prisoner's removal. 'attempted_lynching' or a gathering of masked men fits; 'siege' is not supported
'party of masked men' / 'masked mob'; masked, but no organized band named
Supported: Rosier was in the county jail, removed by the jailer before the mob arrived

info: Saturday night, October 3, 1903 (the Saturday before the Tuesday, October 6, reports); about 10 o'clock per A2
La Plata, Charles County, Maryland; county jail and the woods near La Plata
Melved H. Rosier, a 'colored boy' of fifteen (A1) or 'about 15' (A2), employee of W. B. S. Chapman
Charged with attempted assault on the four-year-old daughter of his employer, W. B. S. Chapman
A 'party of masked men' (A1); a 'masked mob' (A2); none named
Rosier escaped the mob and was removed to a place of safety Sunday; no later report of the charge's outcome was found

sources.note: 'Lynching Attempted': report from La Plata; masked party Saturday night, warden removed the boy from jail, kept in woods, moved to safety Sunday.
quotes: The attempt, it was reported, was made by a party of masked men, but the warden removed the youthful prisoner from the jail in time to frustrate the plan.
